public.description:
Primary WebSocket channel for real-time market data. Clients connect to this
channel to receive order book updates, OHLCV candles, trade executions, and
order status changes.

All communication uses JSON messages. The server sends data updates after
clients subscribe to specific data feeds using the subscribe operation.
public.title: Public Market Data

Error.description:
Sent by the server when a client request cannot be processed. Common causes
include invalid channel names, malformed parameters, or attempting to
unsubscribe from a feed that was never subscribed. The errorName field
provides a machine-readable code for programmatic error handling.

examples.name: subscriptionFailed
examples.summary: Subscription failed due to invalid params

Error.name: Error
Error.title: Error

OHLCVSnapshot.description:
Contains recent OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) candles for the
requested symbol and timeframe. Candles are sorted by timestamp ascending
(oldest first). Use this to populate historical chart data.
OHLCVSnapshot.name: OHLCVSnapshot
OHLCVSnapshot.title: OHLCV Snapshot

OHLCVUpdate.description:
Contains a single candle that was created or updated. If the timestamp matches
an existing candle, replace it (the candle is still forming within its timeframe).
A new timestamp indicates the previous candle closed and a new period started.
OHLCVUpdate.name: OHLCVUpdate
OHLCVUpdate.title: OHLCV Update

OrderUpdate.description:
Sent when the subscribed order's state changes. The `event` field carries
the lifecycle event (`placed`, `reduced`, `filled`, `cancelled`,
`expired`). Fields other than `orderId`, `event`, and `timestamp` are
optional and present only when relevant to the event. On subscribe, the
order's full event history is replayed as a sequence of these updates.
OrderUpdate.name: OrderUpdate
OrderUpdate.title: Order Update

OrderbookSnapshot.description:
Contains aggregated price levels for a market. Each entry has a `price`
and total `quantity` at that price. Bids are sorted by price descending
(highest first), asks are sorted ascending (lowest first). Clients should
use this to initialize their local order book state.

examples.name: orderbookSnapshotExample
examples.summary: SOM:USD order book with 2 bid and 2 ask levels

OrderbookSnapshot.name: OrderbookSnapshot
OrderbookSnapshot.title: Order Book Snapshot

OrderbookUpdate.description:
Contains changed price levels in `bids` and/or `asks`. Each entry has a
`price` and new `quantity`. A quantity of zero means the level was removed
from the book.

Apply updates by replacing the quantity at each price, or removing the
level if quantity is zero.
OrderbookUpdate.name: OrderbookUpdate
OrderbookUpdate.title: Order Book Update

PendingOrderUpdate.description:
Sent when a pending order's state changes. Events:
- `pending_created`: Order registered with trigger price and type.
- `pending_triggered`: Trigger price reached; `success` indicates whether
  the resulting spot order was placed, and `spotOrderId` is the new order ID.
- `pending_cancelled`: Order cancelled before triggering.
PendingOrderUpdate.name: PendingOrderUpdate
PendingOrderUpdate.title: Pending Order Update

Ping.description:
Sent by the client to indicate the connection is still active. The server
responds with a Pong message. Clients should send pings at least every
30 seconds to prevent the 60-second inactivity timeout.
Ping.name: Ping
Ping.title: Ping

Pong.description:
Sent by the server in response to a Ping message. Receipt confirms the
connection is healthy and resets the inactivity timeout.
Pong.name: Pong
Pong.title: Pong

ProtocolError.description:
Sent when a REST-over-WebSocket request cannot be processed due to protocol
issues such as unknown operations, missing required parameters, or server
overload. This is distinct from HTTP errors returned in RestResponse.
ProtocolError.name: ProtocolError
ProtocolError.title: Protocol Error

RestRequest.description:
Sent by the client to invoke a REST API endpoint via WebSocket. The operation
field specifies the OpenAPI operationId (case-insensitive). The server processes
the request through the HTTP handler and returns a RestResponse.

This feature requires the server to be started with REST-over-WS enabled.

examples.name: getTickerRequest
examples.summary: Get market ticker with path parameter

examples.name: prepareOrderRequest
examples.summary: Prepare an order with auth and payload

RestRequest.name: RestRequest
RestRequest.title: REST Request

RestResponse.description:
Sent by the server after processing a RestRequest. Contains the HTTP status
code and response body. The id field matches the request for correlation.
Responses may arrive out of order if multiple requests are in flight.
RestResponse.name: RestResponse
RestResponse.title: REST Response

Shutdown.description:
Broadcast to all connected clients when the server is shutting down gracefully.
Clients should save any pending state and close their connections. Reconnection
attempts should include exponential backoff.
Shutdown.name: Shutdown
Shutdown.title: Shutdown

Subscribe.description:
Sent by the client to subscribe to a data feed. The channel field specifies
which type of data to receive (orderbook, ohlcv, trades, or order). The
params field contains channel-specific parameters like symbols or timeframes.
Subscribe.name: Subscribe
Subscribe.title: Subscribe

Subscribed.description:
Sent by the server to confirm a subscription was activated. Echoes back the
subscription parameters. After receiving this, the client should expect an
initial snapshot followed by incremental updates.
Subscribed.name: Subscribed
Subscribed.title: Subscribed

TradesSnapshot.description:
Contains recent trades for the requested symbol, up to the specified limit.
Trades are sorted by timestamp descending (newest first). Sent immediately
after subscribing to the trades channel.
TradesSnapshot.name: TradesSnapshot
TradesSnapshot.title: Trades Snapshot

TradesUpdate.description:
Contains a single trade that just executed. The side indicates the aggressor
(taker) direction: "buy" means a buy order crossed the spread, "sell" means
a sell order crossed. Sent in real-time as trades occur.
TradesUpdate.name: TradesUpdate
TradesUpdate.title: Trades Update

Unsubscribe.description:
Sent by the client to unsubscribe from a data feed. The params must match
the original subscription parameters to correctly identify which feed to stop.
Unsubscribe.name: Unsubscribe
Unsubscribe.title: Unsubscribe

Unsubscribed.description:
Sent by the server to confirm a subscription was deactivated. After receiving
this, the client will no longer receive updates for the specified data feed.
Unsubscribed.name: Unsubscribed
Unsubscribed.title: Unsubscribed

orderId.description: The order ID to subscribe to

symbol.description: Market symbol the order belongs to (e.g. "SOM:USD")

block.description:
Block number the event was observed in. Present when the source
event carries a block reference; absent for event types that do
not.

expiresAt.description: Unix timestamp (ms) at which the order expires. Orders placed without an explicit expiry carry the server-side default of 24 hours from placement. Absent when the source event did not record an expiry — that means unknown, not "never expires".

isBid.description: Whether this is a buy (true) or sell (false) order.

price.description: Limit price as decimal string, scaled by quote decimals.

quantity.description: Original order quantity as decimal string, scaled by base decimals.

remaining.description: Remaining unfilled quantity as decimal string, scaled by base decimals.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (ms) when the event occurred

depth.description: Number of price levels per side

asks.description: Changed ask price levels. Quantity zero means the level was removed.

bids.description: Changed bid price levels. Quantity zero means the level was removed.

orderId.description: The pending order ID to subscribe to

symbol.description: Market symbol the pending order belongs to (e.g. "SOM:USD")

block.description:
Block number the event was observed in. Present when the source
event carries a block reference; absent for event types that do
not.

isBid.description: Whether this is a buy (true) or sell (false) order. Present on pending_created.

pendingOrderType.description: Type of spot order placed when triggered. Present on pending_created.

spotOrderId.description: The spot order ID created when triggered. Present on pending_triggered when success is true.

success.description: Whether the triggered spot order was placed successfully. Present on pending_triggered.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp (ms) when the event occurred

triggerAbove.description: True if the order triggers when price >= triggerPrice, false for <=. Present on pending_created.

triggerPrice.description: Price that triggers the order. Present on pending_created.

clientTimestamp.description:
Optional client wall-clock at ping-send time (Unix milliseconds,
UTC). Echoed back on the matching `pong` so the client can
compute round-trip latency: `T_received - clientTimestamp`. If
present it MUST be an integer; non-numeric values are rejected
with an `error` message (`errorName: "invalid_request"`).

Echoes the `clientTimestamp` from the matching `ping` when
present. Absent when the ping did not supply one.

serverTimestamp.description:
Server wall-clock at pong-send time (Unix milliseconds, UTC).
Always set. With reasonably synchronized clocks, comparing
this to the client's local read time estimates server→client
delay; comparing to `clientTimestamp` estimates client→server
delay. Round-trip time (`T_received - clientTimestamp`) does
not depend on clock sync.

price.description: Price as decimal string for precision (e.g., "1.23456789")

quantity.description: Aggregate quantity at this price level as decimal string. Zero means the level was removed.

id.description: Client-provided request ID for correlating responses

params.description: Path and query parameters as key-value pairs

since.description: Unix timestamp (ms) to fetch trades from

info.description:
WebSocket API for dreamDEX, providing real-time market data
through subscription-based channels and REST-over-WebSocket RPC.

## Subscription Model

Use `subscribe` and `unsubscribe` operations to manage channel subscriptions:

```json
{"operation": "subscribe", "channel": "orderbook", "params": {"symbols": ["SOM:USD"]}}
{"operation": "unsubscribe", "channel": "orderbook", "params": {"symbols": ["SOM:USD"]}}
```

## REST-over-WebSocket

Invoke any REST API endpoint via WebSocket using OpenAPI operationIds.
This is available when the server is started with a config file.

**Request format:**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "operation": "getMarkets",
  "params": {"symbol": "SOM:USD"},
  "bearerToken": "<token>",
  "payload": {"side": "buy", "amount": "100"}
}
```

**Response format:**
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "status": 200,
  "payload": {"markets": [...]}
}
```

- `id`: Client-provided integer ID for correlating responses (required)
- `operation`: OpenAPI operationId (case-insensitive)
- `params`: Path and query parameters
- `bearerToken`: Bearer token for authenticated requests
- `payload`: Request body for POST/PUT/PATCH

Responses may arrive out of order; correlate by `id`.

## Heartbeat

Send `{"operation": "ping"}` to receive
`{"operation": "pong", "serverTimestamp": <unix-ms>}`. Connections
close after 60 seconds of inactivity.

To measure latency, include a `clientTimestamp` (Unix ms, UTC) on the
ping — the server echoes it back on the pong, alongside its own
`serverTimestamp`, so the client can compute round-trip time as
`T_received - clientTimestamp`.

## Close Codes

The server uses standard and application-specific WebSocket close codes:

| Code | Name | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| 1000 | Normal Closure | Connection closed normally. |
| 1001 | Going Away | Sent on server shutdown *and* on the periodic max-lifetime close (~ every 55 minutes). Reconnect immediately and resubscribe. |
| 4001 | Slow Consumer | Client cannot keep up with the message rate. Reconnect and resubscribe to receive a fresh snapshot. |

Note: connections are proactively closed after a bounded lifetime
(default ~55 minutes) so clients see a clean `1001` close instead of
the abnormal `1006` that infrastructure-enforced timeouts would
otherwise produce. Treat `1001` as normal lifecycle behavior.
info.title: dreamDEX WebSocket API

receivePing.description:
Receives a ping message from the client. The server immediately responds
with a pong message. Clients should send pings periodically to prevent
the connection from timing out after 60 seconds of inactivity.

receiveRestRequest.description:
Receives a REST API request from the client. The operation field specifies
the OpenAPI operationId to invoke. The server processes the request through
the HTTP handler and returns a RestResponse with the result.

This feature is only available when the server is started with REST-over-WS
enabled (requires a config file).

receiveSubscribe.description:
Receives a subscription request from the client. The server validates the
request parameters and, if successful, begins streaming the requested data.
The client receives a subscribed confirmation followed by an initial snapshot,
then incremental updates as data changes.

receiveUnsubscribe.description:
Receives an unsubscription request from the client. The server stops sending
updates for the specified data feed and confirms with an unsubscribed message.

sendError.description:
Sends an error message when a client request cannot be processed. This may
occur due to invalid parameters, unknown channels, or server-side issues.
The message field contains a human-readable error description.

sendOHLCVSnapshot.description:
Sends historical candlestick data immediately after a client subscribes
to the ohlcv channel. Contains recent candles for the requested symbol
and timeframe. Clients should use this to populate charts before
receiving live updates.

sendOHLCVUpdate.description:
Sends a new or updated candlestick as trading occurs. If the candle
timestamp matches an existing candle, the client should replace it
(the candle is still forming). A new timestamp indicates the previous
candle closed and a new one started.

sendOrderUpdate.description:
Sends an event when the subscribed order's state changes. Events are
`placed`, `reduced`, `filled`, `cancelled`, and `expired`. On subscribe,
the order's full event history is replayed as updates, so no separate
snapshot message is sent. Each update carries the event-specific fields
(e.g. `price`, `quantity`, `remaining`) rather than a full order object.

sendOrderbookSnapshot.description:
Sends the complete order book state immediately after a client subscribes
to the orderbook channel. Contains aggregated price levels with total quantity
at each price. Bids are sorted by price descending (highest first), asks are
sorted ascending (lowest first). Clients should use this to initialize their
local order book state before applying incremental updates.

sendOrderbookUpdate.description:
Sends incremental order book changes as they occur. Each update contains
changed price levels in the `bids` and/or `asks` arrays. A quantity of zero
means the level was removed from the book.

Apply updates by replacing the quantity at each price level, or removing the
level if the quantity is zero.

sendPendingOrderUpdate.description:
Sent when a pending (stop) order's lifecycle changes. Events include
`pending_created` (order registered), `pending_triggered` (trigger price
reached and spot order placed), and `pending_cancelled` (order cancelled
before triggering). Subscribe by providing the market symbol and order ID.

sendPong.description:
Sends a pong response to the client after receiving a ping. This confirms
the connection is alive and resets the inactivity timeout.

sendProtocolError.description:
Sent when a REST-over-WebSocket request cannot be processed due to
protocol issues such as unknown operations, missing parameters, or
server overload. This is distinct from HTTP errors which are returned
in RestResponse.

sendRestResponse.description:
Sends the result of a REST API request back to the client. The response
includes the HTTP status code and response body. The id field matches
the original request for correlation.

sendShutdown.description:
Notifies all connected clients that the server is shutting down gracefully.
Clients should close their connections and reconnect to a different server
or retry after a delay. This message is broadcast to all clients before
the server terminates connections.

sendSubscribed.description:
Confirms a successful subscription. Sent immediately after processing a valid
subscribe request. The confirmation echoes back the subscription parameters
so the client can verify which data feed was activated.

sendTradesSnapshot.description:
Sends recent trade history immediately after a client subscribes to the
trades channel. Contains the most recent trades up to the requested limit
(default 100). Trades are ordered by timestamp descending (newest first).

sendTradesUpdate.description:
Sends a trade notification when an order is filled. Each update contains
a single trade with its price, quantity, and aggressor side. Clients
receive this in real-time as trades execute on the exchange.

sendUnsubscribed.description:
Confirms a successful unsubscription. After this message, the client will
no longer receive updates for the specified data feed.
